previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with right-sided chest pain and found to have multifocal pneumonia and acute kidney injury. He had a history of relapsing polychondritis with a recently placed bronchial stent that developed proximal stenosis. Blood and respiratory cultures identified methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus, and he was treated with vancomycin and zosyn. Due to persistent stent narrowing and infection, he underwent bronchoscopy with stent removal and balloon dilation. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic therapy. His infection resolved, kidney function improved, and he was discharged home on IV antibiotics with follow-up in rheumatology and interventional pulmonology.

SUMMARY:
Mr. ___ presents with a mild oropharyngeal dysphagia
primarily related to baseline congenital anatomy, reduced
laryngeal valve closure and discoordination. This resulted in
trace laryngeal penetration with thin and nectar=thick liquids,
but no aspiration. Swallow function likely chronic, and actually
improved from video swallow in ___. At this time, recommend pt
return to baseline diet of thin liquids and regular solids, 
pills
whole one at a time, with thin liquids. The patient was
encouraged to maintain standard aspiration precautions outlined
below. Respiratory illness not likely related to swallow
function; however, it is possible that when the patient has an
acute medical crisis, swallow function may worsen due to
deconditioning, and he may be at increased risk for aspiration,
therefore he will benefit from monitoring during any future
admissions. 
RECOMMENDATIONS:
1. PO diet: thin liquids, regular solids
2. Pills whole with thin liquids, one at a time
3. TID oral care
4. Standard aspiration precautions: 
    - Sit upright in chair for all meals 
    - Do not eat fast, take one bite/sips at a time
    - Remain upright at 90 degrees after eating/drinking for 30
minutes 
5. Reconsult on any future admissions
